gates.claim: on |z| = 1 the ideal tetrahedron is ISOSCELES: the three angles of e^{i theta} are (theta, (pi-theta)/2, (pi-theta)/2), and they sum to pi. This is what collapses Kummer to a one-variable identity there

Lam(theta) + 2 Lam((pi-theta)/2) = Cl_2(theta), and it is exactly the Clausen duplication formula Cl_2(2t) = 2 Cl_2(t) - 2 Cl_2(pi-t) halved -- which the corpus already had as Cl_2_duplication, so the Lean proof is three lines

THE OTHER HALF -- NOW PROVED (Route 73). Im cLiTwoExt(e^{i theta}) = Cl_2(theta), so the Lambda-sum equals the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm form on |z| = 1. When this gate was written that was numerically true but unproved; QOU/Knot/KummerDilogHalf.lean (im_cLiTwoExt_exp, kummer_unit_circle) now proves it, sorry-free. The gate is kept as the numerical control on the statement

SCOPE: this file does NOT reach Vol(5_2). The 5_2 shape y_1 has |y_1| = 1.5236, so it is off the unit circle; its tetrahedron is NOT isosceles and log|z| != 0. The general-z case needs the genuine two-variable argument and is untouched

verdict.proved: Kummer's identity on |z| = 1, BOTH halves: BlochWigner_lob(e^{i theta}) = Cl_2(theta) = Im cLiTwoExt(e^{i theta}), sorry-free, standard axioms. The Lambda-side IS Clausen duplication; the dilogarithm side is same-derivative-plus-basepoint at theta = pi.
not_proved: Vol(5_2) -- the geometric factor of Vol = D is untouched
